slots.caption: Hue adds a dedicated Blueprint styling panel while preserving Unreal's normal graph editing tools.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture a Blueprint Editor with the Hue panel docked, one normal selected node, its graph visible, and clear Instance/Category/Global headings.
slots.alt: Hue panel beside a selected Unreal Blueprint node

slots.caption: Four independent color channels can resolve from different styling scopes on the same node.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture or draw a single Blueprint node with four contrasting visual channels and labels identifying the Instance, Category or Global source of each value.

slots.caption: Nested My Blueprint Categories allow child nodes to inherit selected channels from their parents.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture My Blueprint with Combat, Combat|Weapons and Combat|Weapons|Melee (or an equivalent nested hierarchy) and a graph demonstrating contrasting inherited colors.

slots.caption: The Hue panel updates as compatible Blueprint nodes are selected and styled.
slots.capture_instructions: Record selecting two different compatible graph nodes and using the Hue panel to change an Instance color, then clear it. Keep source labels visible.
slots.alt: Hue Blueprint panel responding to selection

slots.caption: Hue connects Blueprint editing tools, style resolution and native-safe node presentation through editor-only interfaces.
slots.capture_instructions: Draw a diagram showing HueModule, HueStyleResolver, HuePanel, HueMenu, HueNodeFactory/PinFactory and native decorators, with Blueprint assets and project configuration as data owners.

slots.caption: A styled Blueprint graph can distinguish related systems at a glance while preserving native execution and data connections.
slots.capture_instructions: Show a real Blueprint graph with at least three groups of nodes using different Hue colors for identifiable gameplay functions, with wires, titles and the Hue panel visible. Use meaningful colors rather than a random rainbow.
slots.alt: Unreal Blueprint graph with several Hue-styled node groups

slots.caption: Hue can be installed directly in a project's Plugins directory without changing Unreal Engine source.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture Windows File Explorer showing YourProject/Plugins/Hue in the address bar with Hue.uplugin, Source, Resources and Config visible together. Do not show a doubly nested Hue/Hue folder.
slots.alt: Hue plugin installed in an Unreal project Plugins folder

slots.caption: A local Instance override changes only the selected compatible node and can be cleared to reveal its inherited color.
slots.capture_instructions: Record selecting one standard Blueprint function-call node, opening the Hue panel, setting its Instance Header Color through the picker, then clicking Clear. Keep the selected node, panel scope heading, color row and result in view. End on the original inherited/default state.
slots.alt: Hue panel styling and clearing an Instance Header Color

slots.caption: The four Hue channels can be styled independently to distinguish a node's title, title text, body and pin labels.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture one standard K2 function-call node with a red header, white header text, dark-blue body and yellow body/pin-label text. Annotate all four regions and keep native value inputs recognizable.
slots.alt: Annotated Blueprint node displaying Hue's four visual channels

slots.caption: The same Blueprint node can receive a broad Global color, a Category rule and an Instance exception.
slots.capture_instructions: Create three side-by-side Blueprint graph closeups featuring copies/calls of the same logical node. Label the Global rule that affects them all, the Category rule applied to one member group, and a final Instance-only exception with a distinct header color.
slots.alt: Hue Instance Category Global scope comparison

slots.caption: A Hue node immediately adopts the next applicable Category or Global value when a more specific override is cleared.
slots.capture_instructions: Record a supported function-call node with a Global blue Header Color, then apply a Category orange header and an Instance red header. Clear the Instance override to reveal orange; clear Category to reveal blue. Keep the Hue source label visible throughout.
slots.alt: Hue visual style precedence and clear demonstration

slots.caption: Clearing an Instance color reveals the inherited Category color without affecting the node's other channels.
slots.capture_instructions: Record a node with a Category green Header Color and an Instance red Header Color plus an Instance yellow Body Text Color. Clear only Instance Header Color; show the header turning green while yellow body text stays. Then use Clear All Overrides and show the remaining Instance body text reverting.
slots.alt: Hue Clear Color and Clear All Overrides actions

slots.caption: Descendant Blueprint Categories inherit parent style channels until a closer Category supplies an override.
slots.capture_instructions: Record a Blueprint with My Blueprint Categories Combat, Combat|Weapons and Combat|Weapons|Melee visible alongside matching graph nodes. Set Combat Header Color to red, then override Weapons Header Color with orange, and finally clear Weapons; show Melee inherit red again while unrelated channels remain unchanged.
slots.alt: Hue nested Category inheritance updating on graph nodes

slots.caption: A Hue Category style remains associated with its Blueprint member hierarchy after a Category rename.
slots.capture_instructions: Record a Blueprint with styled My Blueprint Categories Attack and Attack|Weapons. Rename the parent Attack to Combat through the native Blueprint Category editing workflow. Show the updated Combat and Combat|Weapons paths and confirm their previously styled nodes retain their Hue colors.
slots.alt: Hue Category rename preserving inherited node colors

slots.caption: Variable Get and Set nodes can share the same Global Variable style because they represent one underlying member identity.
slots.capture_instructions: Show one Blueprint containing Get and Set nodes for the same named variable and an unrelated variable. Apply a recognizable Global Variable Header Color so Get and Set share the color while the unrelated variable remains unchanged. Keep the Hue panel source label visible.
slots.alt: Hue Global Variable style shared by Get and Set nodes

slots.caption: Hue applies its visual channels to different supported Blueprint node families while leaving their native interaction controls intact.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture a graph containing a function-call node, variable Get/Set, event, branch/switch, compact operator and sequence/timeline where compatible. Apply distinct Hue colors but leave pins and value-entry controls visible and readable. Include at least one unsupported reroute node for comparison.
slots.alt: Hue styling across several supported K2 node types

slots.caption: The Hue panel shows available scopes, individual color channels and the source of the effective style for the current selection.
slots.capture_instructions: Capture a single compatible function-call node selected with the full Hue panel docked beside its graph. Expand all three scope sections; ensure all four channel rows, one Override label, one inherited source label and Clear/Clear All controls are readable. Use a node whose Category and Global identities are both valid.
slots.alt: Annotated Hue panel with Instance Category and Global scope controls
